approachQuestion.prompt:
Balanced Delivery Totals. Each node of a non-empty binary tree contains a signed adjustment. Count the root-to-leaf paths whose sum of node adjustments equals target. A leaf has no children. Include both root and leaf values, and return only the number of qualifying paths.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 4(3(-2(-,-),-),1(-,0(-,-))), target=5. Output: 2, for 4+3-2 and 4+1+0. Example 2: Input: 5(-,0(-,-)), target=5. Output: 1, because the root alone is not a leaf. Example 3: Input: -3(-,-), target=-3. Output: 1.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; adjustments lie between -1000000000 and 1000000000; target lies between -200000000000000 and 200000000000000. All path sums fit signed 64-bit arithmetic. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes. Shape is unrestricted; values may be negative or zero.

options.text: Use a depth-first stack carrying the accumulated root-to-node sum. Test equality only at actual leaves, and explore children regardless of the current sum.
options.feedback: Every complete root-to-leaf path has one endpoint leaf, and signed extensions are allowed to increase or decrease its total.

options.text: Copy the complete value path into every child frame. At each leaf scan its path to compute the total and compare with target.
options.feedback: It tests all the right complete paths, so the result is correct. Copying and rescanning paths is unnecessary when a single sum can be carried.

options.text: Use accumulated sums, but discard a branch as soon as its sum exceeds target.
options.feedback: In Example 1 the prefix 4+3=7 exceeds 5 but the next adjustment -2 yields a valid path. This pruning loses it.

options.text: Increment the answer at every visited node whose root-to-node sum equals target, even if that node has children.
options.feedback: For Example 2 both root and its child have sum 5. This counts 2, but there is only one root-to-leaf path.

feedback.reason: Signed path totals forbid pruning on a large prefix, and only complete root-to-leaf paths qualify.
details: Push the root with its value. Pop a node/sum pair; at a leaf compare with target and update the count. Otherwise push each existing child with sum plus its adjustment, using right-before-left order. Never prune on the sign or magnitude of a prefix. Store no path arrays.

Only root-to-leaf sums count. Signed adjustments mean a prefix above target may later fall back, so pruning by sum magnitude is unsound. Pass one scalar path sum with each pending child, not a copied path.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed depth-first sum method let n be the number of nodes and h the height in nodes. What is the tight worst-case pair? Count pending node/sum frames and the count accumulator; exclude the tree and scalar result. Signed 64-bit addition/comparison is constant-time and no paths are copied.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Extend each root path by one edge per node with height-bounded frames.
details: Every node and parent-child extension is processed once. A depth-first pending frontier needs O(h) fixed-size frames; branching shapes can attain that bound.

Each carried sum is precisely the sum on the unique root-to-node route. Testing only leaves gives exactly one test per complete path, and exploring all children preserves paths with negative suffixes.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Every node and parent-child extension is processed once. A depth-first pending frontier needs O(h) fixed-size frames; branching shapes can attain that bound.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
